newsitem.title: USA: OMB, DC officials meet on Clinton plan for city.
newsitem.headline: OMB, DC officials meet on Clinton plan for city.

text.p: District of Columbia Mayor Marion Barry said Wednesday federal and city officials decided to push for congressional passage of a financial revitalization plan for the financially struggling city as early as this spring.

"We decided the federal government is going to try to get legislation passed before summer," Barry said in a press briefing outside Office of Management and Budget headquarters following a closed-door meeting with OMB chief Franklin Raines.

The Clinton administration on January 14 announced a $3.9 billion, five-year plan for Washington, D.C. and said it was ending the $3.56 billion federal payment to the city it would have made over that period.

Under the plan, the White House would assume the city's pension liabilities for police, firefighters, judges and teachers; boost the federal share of the city's Medicaid payments; and take other steps.
Federal aid would be conditioned on the signing of a memorandum of understanding between the federal government, D.C. government, and the city's congressionally mandated financial control board.

"We went over a whole range of issues from prisons to pensions to medicaid," Barry said of the meeting, also attended by members of the control board and D.C. council. "We were trying to see where we all were on these matters. It was a good meeting."

Raines is scheduled to outline the President's revitalization plan for D.C. at Congress' first hearing on the issue set for 0930 EST on Thursday by the House Government Reform Committee's panel on D.C., chaired by Rep. Thomas Davis, R-Va.
